name: Mitho Lolo
subtitle: sweet fennel-scented ghee flatbread, made for Cheti Chand and eaten with plain yogurt

ingredients.qty: 4 tbsp for the dough, plus 5 tbsp for cooking

ingredients.note: traditional, and it cuts the sweetness
keeps the lolo soft the next day

prepNotes: Dissolve the grated jaggery in 1/2 cup warm water and strain it. Jaggery often carries grit that will tear the dough.
Rub the ghee into the flour before any liquid goes in; this moyan is what makes lolo short and flaky.
Rest the dough 20 minutes covered. It is a stiff, sweet dough and needs the time to relax before rolling.

steps.text: Rub 4 tbsp ghee into the atta with your fingertips for a couple of minutes, until the flour holds its shape when pressed in a fist.
steps.tip: This is the step that decides the texture. Skimp on it and you get a sweet chapati, not a lolo.

steps.text: Mix in the fennel, ground cardamom, cracked pepper and salt.
Pour in the strained jaggery water and the milk and bring it together into a stiff dough. Softer than pastry, firmer than roti dough. Add flour by the spoonful if it sticks.
steps.tip: Jaggery loosens the dough as it stands, so err on the firm side now.

steps.text: Divide into 6 balls. Roll each to about 8mm thick and 12cm across, dusting with flour. Thicker than a paratha, and no need to be neat.
Cook on a medium-low tawa for about 2 minutes, until the surface dries and small blisters appear. Flip.
Spoon a tablespoon of ghee around the edge and cook 2-3 minutes a side, pressing gently with a cloth, until both faces are freckled deep brown.
steps.tip: Keep the heat medium-low. Jaggery burns long before the middle of an 8mm bread is cooked.

steps.text: Stack the cooked lolos under a cloth so they steam and soften, and serve warm with plain yogurt or a glass of milk.

storage: Keeps 3 days in an airtight box at room temperature. Mitho lolo is deliberately made to travel and is often eaten cold. Warm briefly on a dry tawa to bring it back.
